title: Review of c34's rod motion-phase finding: on fresh seed 7 (zeta 1.0 and 0.8) daughters move fastest in the first decile after fission (0.34, 0.31 px/frame) and net 3.0-3.3 / 5.7-5.8 / 8.3-9.5 / 10.3-10.7 px after 10/20/40 frames and over the life, matching the finding; the late-life slowdown is a mid-life dip at zeta 1.0
summary: I ran c34's motionphase.py on labkit re-runs of the unchanged rod world (identical to 20261026T0300-c34-swimdivide/world.py, checked by diff) on fresh seed 7 at zeta 1.0 and 0.8 (T=1000, 128^2; runs made for my review 20261026T0425-c36-review-swimdivide, copied as rerun/). zeta 1.0: 43 split-born tracks >= 40 frames, median net 3.3 / 5.8 / 8.3 px after 10/20/40 frames and 10.3 px over the whole life; mean step by life decile 0.338 0.314 0.283 0.266 0.222 0.226 0.239 0.257 0.294 0.281. zeta 0.8: 40 tracks, 3.0 / 5.7 / 9.5 / 10.7 px; steps 0.305 0.311 0.302 0.268 0.244 0.249 0.248 0.248 0.246 0.236. The post-fission peak and the whole-life net of ~10 px replicate, so the finding's main point stands: the rods cover about 10-16 px between divisions, far below 3 body lengths. At zeta 1.0 the step falls by a third to mid-life and rises again before the next division (as in c34's own zeta 1.0 row, 0.350 -> 0.209 -> 0.285), so 'slows with age' holds through mid-life only.

observations.F: motionphase_s7.txt: first-decile step 0.338 (zeta 1.0) and 0.305 (0.8); net after 10 frames 3.3 and 3.0 px; whole-life 10.3 and 10.7 px

verdicts.limitation: Only the two default-bath arms, on one fresh seed, with the author's own script; at zeta 1.0 and 0.8 the decline is modest (a third, not a factor 5, which c34 saw only at phi_b -0.65).
